details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20245-20251, 31272, 31645-31662 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The red|timeout branch of persist_orch_wave_check now keeps `wave_check_wait_since`/`wave_check_wait_head` and relies on the `stale` clear, but incomplete-wave ticks hit `continue` at lines 31645-31646 before the only call site at line 31662, so the fields carry over to the next wave boundary.
  WHY: At the next boundary the stale `pwc_wait` skips the `boundary_first_seen` hold, so pending checks time out at once with a false "still pending after N minutes" judge block, a pre-merge head can advance on green, and no-checks fails open. This is a regression from removing `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear "${pwc_outcome}"`, with no test covering the incomplete-wave path. Four reviewers rated it MAJOR; gemini gave no severity.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20239-20252, 31727-31751 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A persistent red result sets `INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true` and keeps the wait fields on every tick, while the gate's `final_merge_status == "pending"` precondition triggers the final-PR judge-cycle cap bypass (FINAL_PR_PHASE_CAP_BYPASS), so the judge runs every tick with no cap.
  WHY: This means unbounded judge model runs (cost and Actions minutes) and possible tracking-issue spam. luna and glm rated it MAJOR; gemini gave no severity. Disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly rejected this claim, arguing that the same-tick judge advances the wave or adds fix-ups, so the red path is not re-entered every tick.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:736-754 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `classify_check_runs._replaces` lets a newer run supersede a cancelled CI-name run only when both have the same Actions run id, and omits the bound-CI-run clause of `PR_CHECKS_JQ_SUPERSEDE_DEFS` (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh line 119, `PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS`).
  WHY: ci.yml runs on both push and pull_request, so a cancelled `lint` followed by a successful `lint` from the other CI run is classified red and sent to the judge, while the final-merge gate treats it as superseded. All four reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20055 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_persist_orch_wave_check_stamp` still writes the shell global `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_STAMP`, but nothing reads it any more.
  WHY: The dead assignment causes no runtime failure but could mislead maintainers into treating it as part of the contract (rated NIT; sonnet raised the same point as a hardening suggestion only).
- (pre-push test gate results in the PR description; no single hunk maps them) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The PR's pre-push gate attributes 6 failures to this change (tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py, tests/test_persist_postmerge_verify.py::test_phase_labels_mirror_label_helpers_and_label_is_registered, tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py, ruff, shellcheck), and none of them can be tied to a diff hunk.
  WHY: These failures were never confirmed or refuted: ruff was reported as pre-existing, ShellCheck timed out, and CI check-runs were still in_progress. If they are real, CI fails on merge (rated NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: P9 "Any failure: set `INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true` so the existing judge path runs" (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md lines 536-538; line 117 "requires the integration PR's head check runs to be green")
  expected_change_site: scripts/persist_orchestrator.py::classify_check_runs and its invocation in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh::persist_orch_wave_check (line 20160, `--required-names="${ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS-...}"`)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The classifier adds failures only when `mode == "all" or r.get("name") in names` (scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:760-762 / lines 757-763), and the poller passes ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS, so a failed check outside that list gives green and the wave advances without the judge. tests/test_persist_orchestrator.py::test_wave_check_required_names_follow_the_final_merge_gate and tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py::test_persist_orch_wave_check_ignores_failing_checks_outside_the_required_names codify the narrowing. The editor kept this deliberately (advisory copilot-pull-request-reviewer fails persistently), so the plan should be amended, or a human should decide between the plan and the override (sonnet NIT; luna/glm MAJOR).
- requirement: P9 "API: at most 2 calls per wave boundary per tick."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh::persist_orch_wave_check
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: On a red result with an Actions job and `PERSIST_JOURNAL_ENABLED=true`, the poller reads check runs, reads the failing job log (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20213-20215`) and appends the journal (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20278-20281`), which does a GitHub comment write (`scripts/attempt_journal.py:635-638`). That is at least 3 calls (MAJOR).
- requirement: "the wait is bounded per wave boundary, also when the integration PR's head moves" and "the stale clear removes them once the judge advances the wave or adds fix-ups" (changelog.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md, agents.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md "State field" and "Failure modes" bullets)
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh inside `persist_orch_wave_check` (head-move and red|timeout branches) and/or the gate at the function top
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The LAST RUN DIFF replaces `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear "${pwc_outcome}"` with `if [ "${pwc_head_moved}" = "true" ]; then _persist_orch_wave_check_stamp ...` (no clear). The only clear path is the "stale" branch gated on INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK/WAVE_COMPLETE/ANY_FAILED, and none of those fire at a clean boundary after the judge advances the wave (MAJOR).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_orch_wave_check red|timeout branch ~20245-20251; managed loop line 31272, `continue` lines 31645-31646, call site line 31662 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Wait fields kept after red/timeout are cleared only by the `stale` clear inside persist_orch_wave_check, which is unreachable on WAVE_COMPLETE=false ticks. When the judge advances the wave (`.current_wave = NEXT_WAVE`, line 32809) or adds fix-ups, the fields survive to the next boundary.
  WHY: The stale `pwc_wait` skips the `boundary_first_seen` hold and `pwc_head_moved=true` classifies the pre-merge head at once: (a) green advances without checking the merges, (b) pending becomes an immediate `timeout` with a false judge block, (c) no-checks becomes `no_checks_timeout` and fails open. test_persist_orch_wave_check_stale_field_is_removed_when_the_gate_does_not_hold covers only INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true. Fix: call `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear stale` in the `WAVE_COMPLETE != true` branch and add a test.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:classify_check_runs nested `_replaces` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The supersede rule implements only the same-Actions-run half of `PR_CHECKS_JQ_SUPERSEDE_DEFS` (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh line 119) and omits the bound CI run clause (`$rb and _bound_ci_run`, PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS).
  WHY: ci.yml runs on pull_request (line 13-14) and push to orchestrator/project-* (line 16), so a cancelled `lint` plus a successful `lint` gives `red` and a spurious judge call while the final-merge gate supersedes it. Fix: pass bound run ids, or document the difference.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Requirement: docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md line 538 "Any failure: set INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true so the existing judge path runs"; line 117 "requires the integration PR's head check runs to be green".
  Expected change site: scripts/persist_orchestrator.py classify_check_runs (`mode == "all" or r.get("name") in names`) and the poller's `--required-names="${ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS-...}"`.
  Evidence of absence: Failed checks outside ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS are ignored, and tests/test_persist_orchestrator.py asserts green ("ci, lint" maps to green). The narrowing was kept deliberately (copilot-pull-request-reviewer custom_instructions_too_large), so amend the plan or note the departure in the PR body.
- Not reported (explicit rejection): the pass-1 claim of an unbounded per-tick judge on a persistent red. The same-tick judge advances the wave or adds fix-ups, so the red path is not re-entered every tick.
- HARDENING (risk score 3) (3 related items): add `[ -n "${STATE_FILE:-}" ] && [ -f "${STATE_FILE}" ] && _persist_orch_wave_check_clear stale || true` in the WAVE_COMPLETE != "true" branch (line 31272) before line 31646; keep the agents.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md "Failure modes" sentence accurate; make `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_STAMP` in _persist_orch_wave_check_stamp a `local` (e.g. `pwcs_since`).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 31645-31662 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Stale wait fields (`wave_check_wait_since`, `wave_check_wait_head`) may persist across wave boundaries if the stale-gate logic does not explicitly clear them.
  WHY: Old wait timestamps can be misread at the next boundary, which can cause an immediate timeout or a wrong skip decision. The complex control flow makes field carry-over likely.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:line 20247 (persist_orch_wave_check red/timeout branch) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Red results keep the wait fields and re-invoke the judge every tick, with no upper bound, while the final PR is pending.
  WHY: The judge-cycle cap is bypassed when `final_merge_status == "pending"`, so the judge runs every tick on the same failure. This means unbounded model cost and possible tracking-issue spam.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_orch_wave_check head-move and red|timeout branches (around lines 20131-20145 and 20242-20249 in the LAST RUN DIFF); manage loop lines 31272-31649; call site line 31662 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN replaced `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear` in red|timeout with keep-the-fields semantics. The only clear is the gate-fail "stale" branch: it does not fire on clean-wave ticks, and incomplete-wave ticks `continue` at 31645-31646 before line 31662.
  WHY: After the judge advances the wave, the new head is classified against the old wait_since, so it times out immediately with INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true and an `=== BEGIN UNTRUSTED WAVE CHECK ===` block that does not describe the new head. The agents.d/changelog promises do not hold (regression).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_persist_orch_wave_check_stamp (LAST RUN DIFF at the new line 20055: `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_STAMP="${2:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)}"`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_STAMP` is written but no longer read; the timestamp is now passed as an argument.
  WHY: No runtime failure, but it hurts readability and may mislead maintainers.
